chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from his brother al-Hasan from Zura'ah ibn Muhammad from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about a man who divorced his wife while he was ill. He said: 'She inherits him as long as she is in her waiting period. If he divorces her in a state of lingering illness (marad al-mawt), she inherits him for one year. If he exceeds the year by one day, she does not inherit him, and she observes from him four months and ten days, which is the waiting period of the one whose husband has died.'

key_terms.إِضْرَارٍ: Lingering illness (marad al-mawt), a state of terminal illness from which one is not expected to recover.
key_terms.اَلْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا: The one whose spouse has died, referring to the status of the husband in this context.
key_terms.سَنَةٍ: One year, the specific duration for inheritance in cases of divorce during lingering illness.
key_terms.عِدَّتِهَا: The waiting period (iddah) a woman observes after divorce or death of her husband.

ai.seo_question: How long does a wife inherit from her husband if he divorces her while terminally ill?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between general illness and 'lingering illness' (marad al-mawt) in determining a wife's inheritance share, a key topic in Shia jurisprudence. It establishes that if the husband divorces during this terminal phase, the wife inherits for a full year, mirroring the waiting period of a widow, unless the illness persists beyond one year by even a single day, in which case her status reverts to that of a divorced woman. This ruling underscores the principle that death-like illness triggers inheritance rights similar to actual death, protecting the wife's financial security during the transition.
